hypothesis: H1: The copied spatial residual (64x64 grid from the nearest training image, added to every pixel) is what makes the developed RAW look bad, not the global mapping
test: Render 3 Pixel pairs in 4 variants (plain rawler, global quantile map only, global + residual, camera JPEG). Compare MAE vs camera JPEG and view the PNGs. If global-only is as close or closer than global+residual, H1 is supported
notes: 8 Pixel pairs (Downloads/other): residual lowers MAE every time (e.g. 0.0553 -> 0.0257, 0.0664 -> 0.0430). Visually PXL_20260806_114652240 full develop is very close to the camera JPEG. Residual is not the cause on these files. Caveat: these pairs may be in the training set (in-sample).

hypothesis: H2: The learned mapping only works on RAWs close to its training set. On unseen RAWs (other cameras / no paired JPEG) the nearest-prototype target curves are wrong and the develop comes out bad
test: Develop an unpaired RAW (Downloads/other/IMGP4269.DNG, Pentax, no camera JPEG). Check the nearest-prototype distance and view the develop next to the plain render
notes: Nearest prototype distance 1.34 (the spatial residual cutoff is 0.18, so it is skipped). Developed image has colored speckle and a blue/yellow cast; plain render is clean but dark. Out-of-distribution input gets a wrong global curve.

hypothesis: H3: On unseen images the learned per-channel curves lift the shadows too much and too unevenly. The blue channel gets lifted most, which amplifies its sensor noise into the colored speckle
test: Print per-channel median (plain vs developed) for IMGP4269 at 1024 px. If the developed/plain gain is much larger for blue than for red and green, and far above what the image needs (median ~0.5), H3 is supported
notes: Median plain R,G,B = 0.104, 0.033, 0.008; developed = 0.213, 0.178, 0.132. Gain R 2.0x, G 5.5x, B 16.7x. Blue (noisiest, darkest channel) is lifted by far the most, so the speckle is per-channel amplification of noise and a color cast from unrelated neighbour curves.

hypothesis: H4: The learned model is OOD for every non-Pixel camera. Its training set is Pixel-only (341 Pixel DNG/JPEG pairs), and load_render_target only pairs Pixel naming, so Sony/other pairs never reach the training or probe targets
test: Develop Sony ARW files from Pictures/2026/2026-08-09 and compare against their same-name SOOC JPG (not the embedded preview). Report nearest-prototype distance and MAE for plain, global, full. If distances are large and full MAE is much worse than on Pixel pairs, H4 is supported
notes: Sony set (Pictures/2026/2026-08-09, 12 ARW): nearest-prototype distance 0.27-0.50, all above the 0.18 residual cutoff. load_render_target only pairs Pixel naming, so these SOOC JPGs were never used for training or the old probe. Learned global MAE vs SOOC 0.041-0.153 (worse than plain on DSC03865/66 and 03873 is close).

hypothesis: H5: A simple develop with no learned data (one exposure gain set from the image median, applied equally to R,G,B, then a fixed hue-preserving tone curve on luminance, then sRGB encode) avoids the cast and speckle and matches the SOOC JPEG at least as well as the learned mapping, on Sony, Pixel and Pentax
test: Add develop_simple_u16 as a candidate. Compare MAE vs SOOC on the Sony set against the learned global variant, and view the Pentax and a Sony frame. If it is as good or better on both and has no cast/speckle, H5 is supported
notes: Pentax IMGP4269 (unseen): simple develop removes the blue speckle and cast; reads as a natural sunset. Sony set MAE vs SOOC: simple wins 6/12 frames, learned wins 6/12, mean close. Pixel pairs: simple is farther from the phone JPEG (0.08-0.24 vs 0.02-0.04 learned) but visually natural; learned numbers are in-sample. Decision: simple develop is the universal fix.

hypothesis: H6: The Sony develops are low contrast because the tone curve is a gentle shoulder with no toe/S-shape: midtones stay compressed (0.18 linear maps to 0.154) and the tonal spread is much narrower than the SOOC JPEG
test: Measure sRGB luma percentiles (p5, p50, p95) and std for develop_raw_u16 vs the same-name SOOC JPG on the Sony frames. If the develop spread is clearly narrower than SOOC (about 20%+), H6 is supported
notes: Sony 12 frames (develop vs SOOC): p5 0.216 vs 0.104 (blacks lifted), p50 0.428 vs 0.342 (median pinned to mid grey), p95 0.777 vs 0.772, std 0.167 vs 0.198. Spread p5-p95 is 16% narrower. Cause: exposure pinned to a fixed median lifts the shadows, and the shoulder-only curve adds no midtone contrast.

hypothesis: H7: Auto-levels on the 1st and 99th luminance percentiles, one S-curve (strength 0.5) and gamma 0.63 on the mapped luminance (hue-preserving, same for all channels) match the SOOC tone distribution on Sony frames without the fixed median pin
test: Sony 12 frames: compare p5/p50/p95/std of develop vs SOOC. Then view DSC03865 and the Pentax IMGP4269 develop
notes: Averages dev vs SOOC: p5 0.103 vs 0.104, p50 0.339 vs 0.342, p95 0.800 vs 0.772, std 0.205 vs 0.198. DSC03865 looks close to SOOC; Pentax sunset is vivid with no speckle. Note: the 99.9th percentile was too high (sun/specular outliers squeezed the image), so 99% is used. SOOC is somewhat more saturated in greens (not addressed).

hypothesis: H8: Highlights clip because each channel is clamped to 1.0 separately after the luminance scale. Bright pixels with one channel above 1 lose their chroma ratio, so the hue drifts toward yellow/white and the clipped area is larger than in SOOC
test: Measure the fraction of pixels with any channel at 255 (8-bit) and the mean hue of bright pixels (luma > 0.8) for develop vs SOOC on the Sony frames, plus the Pentax sunset. If develop clips much more and the bright hue differs, H8 is supported
notes: Desaturate-on-overflow was added. Sony clip (any 8-bit channel = 255) stayed 0.0349 vs SOOC 0.0027, and bright-pixel hue barely changed. So the per-channel clamp was not the main source. Clipping comes from the levels/tone top end: 99th percentile maps to 1 by design, and s_curve+gamma push values near 1 to 255 in 8-bit. Next: measure that source directly.

hypothesis: H9: Highlights clip because the top of the luminance range has no shoulder. The 99th percentile maps to exactly 1.0 and s_curve+gamma push everything above it to white, so bright areas (sky, sun, white surfaces) go flat and the 95th percentile is too hot
test: Same probe on Sony (12), Pixel pairs (12, vs phone JPEG) and Pentax. Compare clip fraction and p95 with the reference. If develop p95 is above the reference and clip is several times higher, H9 is supported. Then add a soft shoulder above a knee and re-measure
notes: Soft shoulder above knee 0.8 helped a little: Pixel clip 0.0757 -> 0.0670, Sony 0.0349 -> 0.0317. The main clipping source was not the top of the luminance range. Kept as a gentle roll-off.

hypothesis: H10: The remaining clip comes from the luminance-ratio scale. Scaling every channel by mapped/luma pushes a saturated channel (orange sun/sky, red roofs) above 1.0; the desaturation then turns it into 255. Scaling by the brightest channel instead keeps max <= 1 by construction, so nothing overflows and hue is kept
test: Replace the luma input of the tone with the max channel, drop the desaturation branch, and re-run the all-set probe. If clip falls on Sony, Pixel and Pentax and p95 approaches the references, H10 is supported
notes: Scaling by the brightest channel (scale = mapped(max)/max) removes overflow by construction. Clip: Sony 0.0027 (SOOC 0.0027), Pixel 0.0004 (phone 0.0036), Pentax 0.037 (white sun only). Sony p5/p50/p95/std 0.098/0.334/0.761/0.194 vs SOOC 0.104/0.342/0.772/0.198. Pentax p50 darker (0.213 vs 0.252); the sunset is richer and not blown out. Visual check: Pixel and Pentax look natural.

hypothesis: H11: Max-channel scaling removes clipping but darkens saturated scenes (Pentax p50 0.252 -> 0.213). Using the luminance ratio, but capped so the brightest channel stays <= the mapped value, should keep the tone where it fits and only compress pixels that would overflow
test: scale = min(mapped/luma, mapped/max). Re-run all-set probe. Pass if clip stays near the references and Pentax p50 returns to about 0.25 while Sony/Pixel keep their numbers
notes: min(luma scale, 1/max) reclipped the Sony set (clip 0.0317) and Pentax (0.182): the luminance scale overflows many saturated pixels, so a cap alone just turns them white. The brightest-channel scale is the fix.

hypothesis: H12 (final): The clipping fix is the brightest-channel scale with a soft shoulder above 0.8 and the levels from H7. Check that Sony, Pixel and Pentax all improve without losing the contrast fixed in H7
test: all_probe on the three sets, then visual check of a Pixel and a Pentax frame
notes: Final: Sony clip 0.0027 (SOOC 0.0027), p95 0.761 (SOOC 0.772). Pixel clip 0.0004 (phone 0.0036), p95 0.836 (phone 0.787), MAE 0.098 (in-sample learned was 0.02-0.04, not comparable). Pentax clip 0.037, sun is the only white. All 61 tests pass.

hypothesis: H13: The develop is less colorful than the reference camera JPEGs. Chroma (mean of max-min RGB) is lower on Sony and Pixel, so a single saturation boost after the tone should close the gap
test: Mean chroma (max-min over RGB, 0-1) for develop vs reference on Sony (12) and Pixel (12), plus p5/p50/p95 and clip. If develop chroma is clearly lower than the reference (about 10%+), H13 is supported
notes: Mean chroma is already higher than the reference: Sony 0.100 vs 0.092, Pixel 0.115 vs 0.105. Saturation is not too low on average. The earlier green impression is not visible in the mean, so it is left alone.

hypothesis: H14: The Pixel highlights run hot (p95 0.836 vs 0.787) because the white point sits at the 99th percentile and the knee is at 0.8. Lowering the knee (or the white percentile) should pull p95 toward the reference without adding clipping
test: Same probe after H13. Try KNEE 0.7. Pass if Pixel p95 moves toward 0.79 and clipping stays near the reference

hypothesis: H15: The white point at the 99th percentile is what leaves the Pixel top too bright (p95 0.824 after the knee change, reference 0.787). Moving the white point to the 98th percentile should compress the top and bring p95 down, at the cost of a little more clipping
test: Same probe with WHITE_PERCENTILE 0.98 (KNEE 0.7). Pass if Pixel p95 approaches 0.79 while Sony p95 stays near 0.77 and clip does not rise above the reference
notes: WHITE 0.98 brightened everything: Pixel p95 0.850 (was 0.824), Pixel p50 0.407 (ref 0.391), Sony p50 0.371 (ref 0.342). A lower white point stretches the levels, so it is the wrong direction. Next: test 0.995.

hypothesis: H16: A higher white point (99.5th percentile) gives a gentler stretch, so the top and the midtones both come down. That should lower Pixel p95 and p50 toward the reference, while Sony p50 moves toward 0.342
test: Same probe with WHITE_PERCENTILE 0.995 (KNEE 0.7). Pass if Pixel p95 and p50 move toward 0.79/0.39 and Sony p50 approaches 0.34 without clipping rising
notes: WHITE 0.995: Sony p50 0.305 (ref 0.342) and p95 0.711 (ref 0.772) are too dark; Pixel p95 0.803 (ref 0.787) is closer. The two references want different white points, so no single percentile matches both. Keep 0.99 as the balanced choice.

hypothesis: H17 (final): KNEE 0.7 with WHITE 0.99 lowers clipping and the Pixel highlights without a visible darkening of Sony. Pass if clip is at or below reference on both sets and no p50 moves more than 0.01
test: Final round7_probe run on Sony, Pixel and Pentax

hypothesis: H18: The universal develop is manufacturer-independent. It produces sane output (decodes, no crash, clipping and exposure in range) on Canon CR3, Fuji RAF, Olympus ORF, Nikon NEF and Panasonic RW2 samples that it was never tuned on, and the result is reasonably close to each camera's embedded JPEG
test: Add env-gated dataset test over datasets/raw-samples. For each file: develop, report p5/p50/p95, clip, and MAE vs the embedded camera JPEG. Pass if all decode, clip stays low and no file is an outlier

hypothesis: H18: The universal develop is manufacturer-independent (sane output on Canon CR3, Fuji RAF, Olympus ORF, Nikon NEF, Panasonic RW2)
test: dataset test over datasets/raw-samples
notes: Canon CR3, Nikon NEF, Olympus ORF and Panasonic RW2 develop correctly (Nikon/Olympus/Panasonic close to the embedded JPEG, MAE 0.06-0.12). Fuji X-T3 RAF comes out with a strong green cast (dev p50 0.547 vs ref 0.398, MAE 0.221). The dataset surfaced a real decoder bug.

hypothesis: H19: The Fuji green cast is rawler 0.7.2 demosaicing X-Trans with the Bayer PPG algorithm. rawler 0.8.0 adds SensorType detection and XTransBilinearDemosaic, so bumping the dependency fixes Fuji without breaking other cameras
test: Bump rawler to 0.8.0, rebuild, re-run the dataset test (Fuji should be neutral) and the Sony/Pixel/Pentax probes (no regression)
notes: rawler 0.8.0 adds SensorType detection and XTransBilinearDemosaic. Bump compiled with no API change. Fuji X-T3 MAE 0.221 -> 0.190 and the green cast is gone (the blue Yerba Mate package renders blue). No regression: Sony p5/p50/p95 0.098/0.334/0.755 clip 0.0003 MAE 0.0521; Pixel 0.095/0.384/0.823 clip 0.0000 MAE 0.0971; Pentax 0.031/0.212/0.448 clip 0.0193 - all effectively identical to before the bump.

hypothesis: H20: The universal develop is sane across 18 manufacturers/formats (Apple DNG, Canon CR3, DJI DNG, Epson ERF, Fuji RAF, Google DNG, Hasselblad 3FR, Kodak DCR, Leica DNG, Minolta MRW, Nikon NEF, Olympus ORF, OM System ORF, Panasonic RW2, Pentax PEF, Phase One IIQ, Samsung SRW, Sony ARW)
test: dataset test over the expanded set
notes: All 18 develop, clip < 0.001 on every file. Findings: SRW and IIQ were absent from RAW_EXTS so those files were invisible (added crw/dcs/tfr/iiq). rawler cannot decode Sigma X3F or GoPro GPR (excluded). Kodak DCS760C develop shows a yellow-green cast (old DCR, likely no usable as-shot WB). Leica M10 has no embedded JPEG and Canon CR3's extracts black.

hypothesis: H21: Restricting the MAE bench to files with a usable reference (sidecar JPEG, or an embedded JPEG >= 512 px and not black) gives trustworthy MAEs, unlike the earlier numbers which used 160x120 thumbnails for Fuji, Panasonic and DJI
test: reference_bench_runs over datasets/raw-samples, Sony ARW sidecar folder and Pixel DNG folder
notes: Skipped 5 of 18: Canon CR3 (all previews extract black), X-T3 160x120, GX800 160x120, Osmo Action 192x144, Leica M10 no preview. Results: Sony ARW n=36 mean 0.0869 median 0.0606 (true SOOC sidecars); Pixel DNG n=45 mean 0.0964 median 0.0859 (phone preview); mixed n=13 mean 0.1182 median 0.0833 (camera previews, least reliable).

hypothesis: H22: The Sony outlier MAEs are a bench bug, not a develop bug: the bench loaded sidecar JPEGs with image::open (which ignores EXIF orientation) while the develop applies orientation, so portrait frames were compared rotated
test: Apply crate::imgload::orient_preview to sidecar references and re-run the bench on the Sony sidecar set
notes: Sony mean MAE 0.0869 -> 0.0664, median unchanged 0.0606 (the median frame was not portrait). DSC03888 went from 0.2619 to a normal value once oriented. This was the single biggest correction of the whole exercise.

hypothesis: H23: A sweep over the five tone numbers (black, white, contrast, gamma, knee) scored by image-pooled MAE over Sony ARW + Pixel DNG + mixed samples finds an interior optimum that beats the hand-set defaults on the reliable groups
test: tone_sweep at 160 px over ~2000 combinations (rayon + LUT + precomputed luma, ~25 s). Then verify at 512 px with reference_bench
notes: Optimum black=0.005 white=0.95 contrast=0.30 gamma=0.75 knee=0.10, same under pooled and group-mean objectives. At 512 px: Sony 0.0664 -> 0.0592, Pixel 0.0964 -> 0.0870, mixed 0.1182 -> 0.1196. Flat-image MAE floor is 43/255 = 0.17, so this is not a degenerate flat solution. Mixed is heterogeneous (camera previews with own picture styles) and a few files regress (kr 0.073 -> 0.126, nx300 0.078 -> 0.154) as Sony/Pixel improve.

hypothesis: H24: A local-tone stage (blend the global tone with tone applied to a wide box-blurred local base) lowers MAE, even though the worst Sony frames looked like a global rather than local mismatch
test: Add ToneParams.local, tone on the box-blurred base, and sweep local in the tuner
notes: The sweep ranked local=0.5 best in the top 5. At 512 px: Sony 0.0592 -> 0.0557 (median 0.0506 -> 0.0488), Pixel 0.0870 -> 0.0850, mixed 0.1196 -> 0.1185 (median 0.1178 -> 0.1035). Worst Sony DSC03893 0.1564 -> 0.1315. No halos (base is max(w,h)/32, low frequency). Clipping rose from 0 to at most 1.7% (Samsung NX300) because white moved 0.95 -> 0.97; references clip up to 15%, so this is acceptable.

hypothesis: H25: Refining the local-tone operator (finer base and weaker blend) lowers MAE further within the fixed-operator constraints
test: Sweep local and radius_div with the other five numbers frozen, then verify at 512 px
notes: Best local=0.3 radius_div=6 (base max(w,h)/6). At 512 px: Sony 0.0557 -> 0.0537 (median 0.0488 -> 0.0466), Pixel 0.0850 -> 0.0844, mixed 0.1185 -> 0.1157 (median 0.1035 -> 0.0991). No halos on DSC03893/DSC03869. Clipping max 1.6%.

hypothesis: H26: A fitted fixed global per-channel curve (profile-like 3x1D LUT) would substantially reduce MAE
test: Fit per-channel dev->reference LUTs on the pairs and measure MAE before/after, in-sample and cross-camera
notes: At 384 px: Sony 0.0519 -> 0.0531 (worse), Pixel 0.0787 -> 0.0775 (negligible), Sony-fitted LUT on Pixel 0.0785 (no transfer). The levels already match the marginal distribution, so the residual is not a fixed global colour/tone shape. This option is dead.

hypothesis: H27: Per-frame exposure/contrast predicted from the frame's own statistics (percentiles, std, skew) can capture a large part of the 46% per-image headroom, without any scene classifier
test: Ridge regression features->(gain,offset) fit on the pairs, evaluated leave-one-out, on Sony / Pixel / pooled
notes: Sony LOO 12.42 -> 9.16 (-26%, oracle 5.75); Pixel 18.76 -> 18.23 (-3%); mixed LOO 25.91. Out-of-sample transfer, rule fit on sony+pixel and applied to the 13 mixed cameras: 27.74 -> 24.73 (-11%). So a per-frame rule from the frame's own statistics generalizes to unseen cameras, better than a within-mixed fit (only 13 samples). Caveat: needs the pairs to define the target; it is a small learned metering regression, not a scene classifier.

hypothesis: H28: A small fixed linear metering rule (9 statistics of the frame -> gain + offset, coefficients baked in) reduces MAE at runtime with no reference and no model file
test: Implement meter_u16, fit coefficients offline from the pairs, bake, and run the 512 px bench
notes: At 512 px: Sony 0.0537 -> 0.0454 (-15%), Pixel 0.0844 -> 0.0807 (-4%), mixed 0.1157 -> 0.1021 (-12%). Clipping fell to 0.6% max; all 18 cameras stay sane (p50 0.32-0.51). Luma-plane LOO on Sony 12.43 -> 9.16; out-of-sample transfer to 13 unseen cameras -11%. Coefficients clamp to gain 0.6-1.8 and offset -30..+30 luma. Corrects luma only. Some individual frames regress (D850, A1).

hypothesis: H29: The reported Sony frames are under-exposed (bias -30..-48) because the per-frame levels normalize away absolute scene brightness, and the metering (toned-frame features only) cannot recover it. Adding raw-decode statistics (absolute level) as features, and fitting on all four Sony folders instead of one, fixes them
test: Add raw luma percentiles/mean/std as metering features, refit on 2026-07-29/08-06/08-07/08-09, measure at 512 px
notes: Sony LOO 13.59 -> 7.22 of 255 (oracle 6.21); all-74 mean MAE 0.0572 -> 0.0440, median 0.0487 -> 0.0411. Reported frames: DSC03759 0.155 -> 0.071, DSC03764 0.129 -> 0.061, DSC03781 0.125 -> 0.051, DSC03791 0.107 -> 0.035, DSC03792 0.070 -> 0.038, DSC03795 0.134 -> 0.051, DSC03799 0.173 -> 0.051. Pixel 0.0807 -> 0.0786 and mixed 0.1021 -> 0.1008 also improved. Caveat: stricter cross-camera transfer (fit on Sony+Pixel, test on the 13 mixed cameras) got worse (25.4 -> 29.7), i.e. the raw-level relationship is body-specific.

hypothesis: H30: The stronger metering brightens so much that saturated highlights clip per channel (DSC03799 24% vs reference 12%)
test: Cap the correction using the frame's max-channel distribution so at most 12% of pixels clip, trimming offset then gain
notes: Max clip across the 74 Sony frames fell 0.234 -> 0.128 (reference max 0.116); frames over 15% clip went 3 -> 0; mean MAE cost 0.0432 -> 0.0440. A luma-based guard did nothing because the clipping is per channel (saturated sky).

hypothesis: H31: The metering's gain hard-clips bright skies (DSC03800 13.4% clipped, reference 7.7%) while midtones stay dark, because a gain+gamma map cannot lift midtones without pushing highlights over
test: Give the metering the same soft shoulder the tone uses (asymptote to 1.0) instead of a hard clip, then re-measure
notes: DSC03800 clip 13.4% -> 7.3% (ref 7.7%) and p50 0.445 -> 0.491 (ref 0.537); DSC03799 clip 13.7% -> 6.4%, p50 0.440 -> 0.484; DSC03791 clip 9.3% -> 2.2% (ref 4.8%). Sony mean 0.0442 -> 0.0445 (flat); Pixel 0.0786 -> 0.0777. Highlights now roll off instead of clipping.

hypothesis: H32: The metering's shadow lift multiplies sensor chroma noise into visible blue/red speckle (DSC03791 dark hair). The raw decode is clean; the tone alone is clean
test: Save the decode, tone and final images for DSC03791 and compare; add a dark-weighted chroma-only denoise
notes: The decode and tone-only renders are clean, the metered one is not. A chroma-only box blur blended in by (1-luma)^2 strength 0.85 removes the speckle with no measurable MAE change (Sony 0.0442 -> 0.0442). Luma untouched.

hypothesis: H33: Tuning the develop by minimising MAE flattens it - L1 regresses to the conditional median, so contrast and brightness drift toward the middle
test: Aggregate dev-vs-JPEG 5/50/95 luminance percentiles over the 74 Sony pairs; add a percentile term to the sweep objective and relax the metering shoulder (METER_KNEE 0.75 -> 0.95)
notes: Sony dP95 -0.037 -> -0.000, dP50 -0.006 -> +0.017, frames >0.01 dark 32/74 -> 16/74, MAE 0.0445 -> 0.0442, clipping +1.7%. Mixed group regresses 0.0990 -> 0.1078 (its references are embedded previews).

hypothesis: H34: The camera JPEG is the wrong absolute target - matching it leaves subjects dark next to modern expectations, and applying AUTO to a JPEG over-crunches an already-punchy input
test: Add a small global lift to the metering (METER_BRIGHTEN = 10) and drop the Auto seed's baseline contrast (18 -> 10), then re-measure against the JPEGs
notes: Develop dP25 +0.073, dP50 +0.057, dP95 +0.034 vs the JPEGs; frames >0.02 dark 10/74 -> 4/74; clipping +2.9%; Sony MAE 0.0442 -> 0.0607 (deliberately off-target now). Auto baseline contrast 18 -> 10 pulls the JPEG+AUTO result back toward the camera's softer look.

hypothesis: H35: Brightening the develop is not free - a gamma low enough to lift midtones also lifts the blacks, and a relaxed shoulder plus a large lift clips highlights, so the frame reads bright but flat (reported as 'way too little contrast')
test: Sweep contrast/gamma/shoulder/lift on the reported frames, measuring p5/p50/p95 against the JPEGs and looking at the images
notes: DSC03795 had p5 0.186 vs the JPEG's 0.119 (lifted blacks). contrast 0.2 -> 0.35, gamma 0.60 -> 0.70, METER_KNEE 0.95 -> 0.80, METER_BRIGHTEN 10 -> 8 gives Sony dP25 +0.024 dP50 +0.003 dP95 -0.017 dClip +0.006 and the best MAE so far (Sony 0.0430, Pixel 0.0778).
